archive: lpmuds.net/files/skylib_fluffos_v3.zip, recovered via Wayback Machine 2026-08-25 (original site down)
name: Skylib
english_description: Version 1.8 of Skylib, an English-language LPMud library boot-banner'd as the "Divided Sky Distribution Lib," in the Discworld/Nightmare lineage: soul-based emotes, a directory-based per-verb command dispatcher, round-time combat, and guilds, built around the same command-dispatch style as Discworld rather than the driver's native add_action(). Content-wise this is an honest work-in-progress skeleton rather than a finished game -- the login banner itself says "this mud is still under construction" -- with no designed adventure zones, only the standard five starting guilds (fighter, mage, thief, cleric, artisan), a training dummy, and a small template area of generic rooms (tavern, garden, shops). Porting it to FluffOS surfaced two especially wide-reaching compatibility bugs beyond the usual .c-to-.lpc rename side effects: this driver build compiles WITH native add_action() support, which the mudlib barely uses, so its own directory-based dispatcher never got control and every single typed command was silently swallowed and doubly rejected with "What?" before the mudlib's real dispatcher ever ran (fixed with a small set of driver-flavor-gated compat shims); and the archive's own bundled include/runtime_config.h used a stale, mismatched get_config() index numbering that silently returned wrong-typed values instead of erroring (replaced with the driver's canonical header). Full registration, login, and the real player command set (look/score/inventory/quit and more) are verified working live. Roughly 127 of 2163 files still fail lpcc's standalone compile sweep, almost all pre-existing content gaps predating this port (deliberately-broken LPC-error teaching examples, mixins that only compile as part of a whole object, a dead/superseded alternate room-topography system, and similar) -- logged in NOTES.md, not fixed, per this project's content-vs-driver-compat scope. Like imud/foundation2, this lib makes a real outbound Intermud-3 socket connection at boot (to a near-certainly-defunct 1990s host) and should not be swept into high-frequency automated re-boot loops.
